questions.q: What does Login As actually do?
options: It opens a real session as another active user, without needing their password, showing exactly what they see
It changes the target user's password so you can log in as them
It simulates access without creating a real session
It only works for inactive users being reactivated
questions.explain: Login As opens a genuine session under the target user's identity — their layouts, access, and UI — and every action in it is logged.

questions.q: Why is Login As not available for an inactive user?
options: Inactive users are automatically deleted
Inactive users never had profiles assigned
There's no session to step into for a deactivated account
It is available for inactive users, with no restriction
questions.explain: A deactivated user can't log in at all, so there's no active session for an admin to step into via Login As.

questions.q: Why does Apex code run in 'system context' by default, and why does that matter for testing?
options: System context means Apex automatically respects every user's sharing rules
System context only applies to Visualforce pages, not Apex
System context disables all Apex tests
System context ignores sharing and field-level security, so a test can pass even though a real user would actually be blocked
questions.explain: Because system context bypasses sharing and FLS, a test that doesn't wrap code in System.runAs() can give a false sense that access controls work as designed.

questions.q: What does System.runAs() do in an Apex test?
options: It permanently changes the running user for the whole org
It executes a block of test code under a specified user's actual sharing permissions
It deletes the test data afterward
It grants the specified user View All automatically
questions.explain: System.runAs() is a test-only construct that applies a specific user's sharing context to the code inside its block, so the test reflects what that real user would actually see.

questions.q: According to the lesson's testing checklist, how should test users be chosen?
options: One real user per role in the design (e.g., one Tier 1 agent, one Regional Manager), not one per individual
One test user per individual person in the org
Only the System Administrator should be tested
Test users should be chosen at random each time
questions.explain: Testing by role rather than by individual keeps the checklist representative and repeatable without requiring a separate test pass for every single user.
